=== NOTES 1:65 | Gupta Religion – Bhagavatism, Vaishnavism, Saivism; Beginnings of Temple Architecture (deogarh, Bhitargaon)
## SUB 0 | Bhagavatism and Vaishnavism
[65:0:0] # Origin
[65:0:1] - **First worshippers of Vasudeva-Krishna:** the **Bhagavatas** (Vasudevakas) (UPPCS 1997) – not Vedic Aryans, Tamils or Abhiras; Vasudeva worship is known from **Panini's** age.
[65:0:2] - **Originator:** **Krishna (Vasudeva)** of the **Vrishni (Satvata)** clan, son of Devaki, pupil of Ghora Angirasa (Chhandogya Upanishad) (RAS 1993) – not Janaka, Yajnavalkya or Surdas.
[65:0:3] - **Earliest epigraphic evidence:** the **Garuda pillar at Besnagar** (Vidisha, c. 2nd c. BCE), set up to Vasudeva by **Heliodorus**, envoy of the Indo-Greek **Antialcidas** at the court of the Sunga **Bhagabhadra** (UKPSC 2012 ×2) – the Prayag prashasti, Nasik and Ayodhya records are later.
[65:0:4] - **Doctrine:** **bhakti**, **ahimsa**, the **avatara** theory – **ten incarnations**; open to women, Vaishyas, Shudras and foreigners.
[65:0:5] # Gupta patronage
[65:0:6] - **Greatest contribution to the Bhagavata sect:** the **Guptas** (State PSC) – virtually the state religion; rulers styled **Parama Bhagavata** (first: **Samudragupta**); dynastic emblem **Garuda**.
[65:0:7] - **Udayagiri (MP):** colossal **Varaha** panel carved under **Chandragupta II**.
[65:0:8] # Avatars and attributes
[65:0:9] - **Varaha (boar):** the incarnation that **saved the Earth from the sea**, lifting her on his tusks after killing **Hiranyaksha** (UP UDA/LDA 2010) – not Matsya, Kurma or Narasimha.
[65:0:10] - **Dashavatara:** Matsya, Kurma, Varaha, Narasimha, Vamana, Parashurama, Rama, Krishna, Buddha, Kalki.
[65:0:11] - **Kaustubha (Kausthubham):** the gem on **Vishnu's chest**, from the churning of the ocean (APPSC Endowment 2022).
[65:0:12] - **Vaishnava symbols:** chakra, shankha, Garuda; **AP angle:** Salankayanas were Vaishnavas (title Parama Mahesvara); Pedavegi inscription of Nandivarman II – first AP record of Vishnu temples.
[65:0:13] ~~ Sources: PMF Ancient & Medieval 03 p.71-72; NextGen Indian History APPSC 03 p.9; app notes 1:65 (sub 1)
## SUB 1 | Saivism, Shaktism and the Puranas
[65:1:0] # Shaiva sects
[65:1:1] TABLE head: Sect | Key facts
  [65:1:1.0] Pashupata | Oldest Shaiva sect; founder Lakulisha
  [65:1:1.1] Kalamukha | Followers of Kalanana (disciple of Lakulisha); extremist; Simha Parishat in Andhra
  [65:1:1.2] Kapalika | Skull-bearing Vamacharas; Bhairava worship; Srisailam a Kapalika kshetra; Bhairavakonda caves
  [65:1:1.3] Mattamayura | A Shaiva sect known from Chedi (Kalachuri) inscriptions (IAS 1996)
  [65:1:1.4] Nathpanth / Lingayats | Matsyendranath, Gorakhnath / Basava
[65:1:2] - **Kapalikas emerged from Misra Saivam** (APPSC G2) – NextGen's APPSC fact list; NextGen's AP history also calls them the Vamacharas of the Kalamukhas. Not Pashupata Saivam, Vaishnavam or Shuddha Saivam in the APPSC key.
[65:1:3] - **Worshippers of Kapalini:** the **Kapalikas** (APPSC Endowment 2022).
[65:1:4] - **⚠ Not a Shaiva sect:** Ajivika (Makkhali Gosala), Mayamata (a text on architecture), Isanasivagurudeva Paddhati (a ritual manual).
[65:1:5] - **Gudimallam** (Tirupati district): earliest known Shiva linga; Gupta **ekamukhalinga** = linga with one face.
[65:1:6] # Shakti
[65:1:7] - **Ardhanarishvara:** half Shiva, half Parvati = the **union of God with his Shakti** (UPPSC 1997).
[65:1:8] - **Mother goddesses:** Durga, Amba, Kali, Chandi; **Tantrism** spread from the **5th century**, open to women and Shudras.
[65:1:9] - **Kalika Purana:** an **upapurana** of **Shaktism**, likely composed in **Assam** (MPPSC 2018 ×2) – not Vaishnava, Buddhist or Jain.
[65:1:10] # Puranas
[65:1:11] - **18 Mahapuranas**; took their final shape in the **Gupta period**; five topics (**pancha-lakshana**): creation, re-creation, genealogies, manvantaras, dynastic history.
[65:1:12] - **Surya worship:** the silk-weavers' guild built a **Sun temple at Mandsaur** under **Kumaragupta I**; Skandagupta's **Indore** plate endows a lamp in a Sun temple.
[65:1:13] - **Kakatiya link:** the **Kalamukha and Pashupata** sects later flourished under the Kakatiyas.
[65:1:14] ~~ Sources: NextGen AP History 04 p.28 (Pasupata, Kalamukha, Kapalika); NextGen AP History 06 p.14 (Kapalikas from Misra Saivam); PMF Ancient & Medieval 03 p.72; app notes 1:65 (sub 2, 3, 4)
## SUB 2 | Gupta Temple Architecture – Deogarh, Bhitargaon and the Panchayatana
[65:2:0] - **Earliest free-standing Hindu temples** survive from the **Gupta** age: square **garbhagriha**, pillared mandapa, raised **jagati**.
[65:2:1] TABLE head: Stage | Examples | Features
  [65:2:1.0] First | Sanchi Temple 17, Tigawa | Flat roof, square sanctum, shallow portico
  [65:2:1.1] Second | Nachna (Parvati), Bhumara (Shiva) | Covered ambulatory, raised platform; Bhumara has two flanking shrines
  [65:2:1.2] Third | Deogarh (Dashavatara, Vishnu), Bhitargaon | Low square shikhara; Panchayatana plan
[65:2:2] - **Dashavatara temple, Deogarh:** in **Lalitpur** district near **Jhansi** (UP); **Gupta** period (APPSC G2 2000) – not Pallava, Chola or Vijayanagara; Vishnu, ten avatars; earliest **Panchayatana** temple of North India.
[65:2:3] - **Panchayatana:** a **style of temple construction** – main shrine plus **four subsidiary shrines** at the corners (UPSC 2014 ×2) – not a village assembly, sect or official.
[65:2:4] - **Deogarh and Garhwa:** the Deogarh temple near Jhansi and the sculptures of **Garhwa** near Allahabad (Prayagraj) are remains of **Gupta art** (State PSC).
[65:2:5] - **Bhitargaon** (near Kanpur): **brick and terracotta** Hindu temple – one of the oldest terracotta temples; not a Buddhist chaitya.
[65:2:6] - **Gupta temple sites:** Deogarh, **Bhitargaon**, **Bhitari** (Ghazipur – Skandagupta's pillar and excavated Gupta Vishnu temples), Nachna, Bhumara, Tigawa, Sanchi, Eran – **Rajgir** is not listed among Gupta temple sites (SI 2018).
[65:2:7] ~~ Sources: PMF Ancient & Medieval 03 p.76, p.86; NextGen Indian History APPSC 03 p.15 (Panchayatan); https://www.cse.iitk.ac.in/users/amit/books/jayaswal-2001-royal-temples-of.html (Bhitari temples); app notes 1:65 (sub 9)
## SUB 3 | Puranic Deities, Weapons and Mounts
[65:3:0] - **Vajrayudha:** Indra's thunderbolt, made from the **backbone of sage Dadhichi** (APPSC Endowment 2022) – Pashupata was Shiva's weapon, Gandiva Arjuna's bow.
[65:3:1] TABLE head: Name | Meaning
  [65:3:1.0] Nandi | Shiva's bull
  [65:3:1.1] Kalpavriksha | Divine wish-fulfilling tree
  [65:3:1.2] Airavata | Indra's divine white elephant
  [65:3:1.3] Kamadhenu | Holy (wish-fulfilling) cow
[65:3:2] - **Match (CGPSC 2013):** A-3, B-4, C-1, D-2.
[65:3:3] - **Sectarian symbols** on Gupta coins and seals: **linga, trident, bull** (Shaiva); chakra, shankha, Garuda (Vaishnava); Gaja-Lakshmi.
[65:3:4] ~~ Sources: NextGen Indian History APPSC 03 p.9; app notes 1:65 (sub 3, 8)
## SUB 4 | Buddhism, Jainism and Religious Tolerance
[65:4:0] - **Buddhism:** lost royal patronage, overshadowed by Bhagavatism; **Nalanda** founded by **Kumaragupta I**; persecuted by the Huna **Mihirakula**.
[65:4:1] TABLE head: Scholar | Contribution
  [65:4:1.0] Vasubandhu | Abhidharmakosa
  [65:4:1.1] Dinnaga | Founder of Buddhist logic
  [65:4:1.2] Buddhaghosa | Visuddhimagga
[65:4:2] - **Jainism:** **Vallabhi council** (5th c.) under **Devarddhi Kshamashramana** wrote down the **Svetambara** canon; **Mathura** a centre of Jain art; **Kahaum** pillar (Skandagupta) records Jain images.
[65:4:3] - **Tolerance:** Samudragupta let **Meghavarman** of Sri Lanka build a monastery at Bodh Gaya; **Amrakardava**, Chandragupta II's officer, made a grant at Sanchi.
[65:4:4] - **Purusharthas:** dharma, artha, kama, moksha – the first three = **trivarga**; devotional Hinduism replaced sacrificial Brahmanism.
[65:4:5] - **Match:** Jainism – Triratna, Agamas, Mahavira; Buddhism – Ashtanga Margam; Saivism – Linga; Ajivika – Makkhali Gosala; Lingayat – Basava.
[65:4:6] ~~ Sources: PMF Ancient & Medieval 03 p.72; NextGen Indian History APPSC 03 p.3-4, p.9; app notes 1:65 (sub 0, 5, 6, 7, 8)

=== NOTES 1:66 | Gupta Art, Literature, Science and Technology – Kalidasa, Aryabhata, Varahamihira, Ajanta, Mehrauli Pillar
## SUB 0 | Ajanta Caves – Phases, Patrons and Paintings
[66:0:0] # Basics
[66:0:1] - **Ajanta** = **Buddhist** rock-cut caves in **Aurangabad (Chhatrapati Sambhajinagar) district, Maharashtra**, cut in a horseshoe-shaped gorge of the **Waghora river** (UPSC 2021) in the Sahyadri ranges – not Sanchi (Betwa side), Pandu-lena (Nashik) or Amaravati (Krishna).
[66:0:2] - **30 caves** (29 numbered + 15A): **5 chaityas** (9, 10, 19, 26, 29), the rest viharas.
[66:0:3] - Rediscovered in **1819** by British officer **John Smith** on a tiger hunt; **UNESCO World Heritage Site 1983** (with Ellora).
[66:0:4] - Ajanta is famous for **Buddhist cave temples** (Uttarakhand 2006) – Elephanta is Shaiva, Khajuraho Hindu-Jain, Nalanda a monastery-university.
[66:0:5] # Two phases
[66:0:6] TABLE head: Phase | Patron | Caves | Note
  [66:0:6.0] Early (2nd–1st c. BCE) | Satavahanas | 9, 10 (also 8, 12, 13, 15A) | Earliest paintings of historical India – Amaravati style
  [66:0:6.1] Later (5th c. CE) | Vakatakas – King Harishena, minister Varahadeva | 1, 2, 16, 17, 19, 26 … | Most paintings and sculpture
[66:0:7] - Ajanta's art was **mainly patronised by the Vakatakas** (Jharkhand 2013) – not Chalukyas, Pallavas or Gangas; the Vakataka phase is contemporary with the **Gupta** age, so "Ajanta built in the Gupta period" (SSC 2014) is the accepted answer.
[66:0:8] - **Earliest paintings** (APPSC AP History PYQ) = **Satavahana** period, Caves 9 and 10 (prehistoric rock art such as Bhimbetka aside).
[66:0:9] # Caves and panels
[66:0:10] TABLE head: Cave | Panel / fact
  [66:0:10.0] 10 | Shwetagaja (Chhaddanta) Jataka – first "completely evolved" painting (APPSC G2 2012)
  [66:0:10.1] 1 | Bodhisattva Padmapani ("lotus-holder"), Vajrapani, Black Princess (Krishna Yuvarani)
  [66:0:10.2] 16 | Dying Princess; excavated by Varahadeva
  [66:0:10.3] 17 | Mother and Child, Bhava-chakra (wheel of life)
  [66:0:10.4] 19 | Chaitya; standing Buddha
  [66:0:10.5] 26 | Mahaparinirvana – a sculpture, not a painting
[66:0:11] - **Black Princess = Cave 1 = Vakataka** phase (late 5th c.) – **not** Satavahana; she is neither the earliest nor the "first" painting (APPSC Welfare 2017 keys gave Satavahana).
[66:0:12] - **Padmapani** = **Avalokiteshvara** (UPSC 1997); his painting is the most famous at **Ajanta** (UPSC 2017) – not Bagh, Badami or Ellora.
[66:0:13] # Themes and technique
[66:0:14] - Themes: **Jataka tales** (Buddha's previous births) and the **life of Gautama Buddha** (SSC 2019; APSC 2017; MPPSC 2012) – not the epics, Panchatantra, Vikramaditya or Mahavira; also court and secular life.
[66:0:15] - Technique: **tempera on dry lime plaster (fresco secco)**, not true fresco; red outlines first.
[66:0:16] - Mural paintings: **Ajanta and Lepakshi** – not **Sanchi** (UPSC 2013).
[66:0:17] - Ajanta vs **Mahabalipuram**: only the **rock-cut** form is common – different periods and religions (UPSC 2016).
[66:0:18] - UPSC 2014 pairs: **Mahaparinirvana – Ajanta** ✓; **Arjuna's Penance – Mamallapuram** ✓; **Varaha rescuing Earth – Udayagiri** (not Mount Abu) ✗.
[66:0:19] ~~ Sources: NextGen Indian History APPSC Part 3 p.13, p.19 (Ajanta paintings, Jataka themes, Dying Princess, Mother and Child); PMF Art & Culture Part 1 (Ajanta, Vakataka phase); https://www.understandupsc.com/?p=8506 (Black Princess Cave 1); app notes 1:66 (sub 9)
## SUB 1 | Dramatists, Fables and Other Authors
[66:1:0] # Dramatists
[66:1:1] TABLE head: Dramatist | Works

[66:1:3] - In Gupta-age Sanskrit plays **women and Shudras speak Prakrit**, kings and Brahmins Sanskrit (IAS 1995).
[66:1:4] - **Court language** of the Guptas = **Sanskrit** (SSC 2000).

## SUB 2 | Scientists – Aryabhata, Varahamihira, Brahmagupta, Bhaskara
[66:2:0] TABLE head: Scientist | Works | Known for
  [66:2:0.0] Aryabhata | Aryabhatiya (499 CE) | First to treat mathematics as a distinct subject (Ganitapada) (APPSC 2010); Earth rotates on its axis → day and night (State PSC); cause of eclipses; pi = 3.1416; decimal place value (UPPSC 2014)
  [66:2:0.1] Varahamihira (6th c., Avanti) | Panchasiddhantika, Brihat Samhita, Brihat Jataka | Astronomy, astrology; termites as a sign of underground water
  [66:2:0.2] Brahmagupta (598–668) | Brahmasphutasiddhanta, Khandakhadyaka | Rules for zero and negative numbers; anticipated Newton – all things gravitate to the earth (UPSC 1995); cyclic quadrilaterals
  [66:2:0.3] Bhaskara I | Commentary on Aryabhatiya | Circle for zero, 629 CE
  [66:2:0.4] Bhaskara II (12th c.) | Siddhanta Shiromani | Algebra (Bijaganita) (UPPCS 2002); Lilavati = mathematics (APPSC G2 2000; State PSC)
  [66:2:0.5] Mahavira (9th c.) | Ganitasarasangraha | Mathematics
[66:2:1] # Varahamihira's texts
[66:2:2] - **Panchasiddhantika** = summary of **5 siddhantas** – Surya, **Romaka**, **Paulisa**, Vasishtha, Paitamaha – based mainly on **Greek** astronomy (State PSC).
[66:2:3] - **Romaka Siddhanta** deals with **astronomy** (APPSC G2), with Roman-Greek influence.
[66:2:4] - **Brihat Samhita** = an **encyclopaedic** work (IAS 1993) – astronomy, astrology, geography, botany, architecture; Amarakosha is a lexicon, Siddhantasiromani mathematics, Ashtangahridaya medicine.
[66:2:5] - **Brihat Jataka** = astrology. **Amarakosha** is by **Amarasimha**, not Varahamihira (CGPSC 2022).
[66:2:6] - **Siddhanta Shiromani** has four parts: **Lilavati**, **Bijaganita**, Ganitadhyaya, Goladhyaya.
[66:2:7] # Zero and place value
[66:2:8] TABLE head: Item | Fact
  [66:2:8.0] Decimal place value credited to | Aryabhata
  [66:2:8.1] Zero arithmetic | Brahmagupta
  [66:2:8.2] Earliest epigraphic place value | Mankani (Sankheda) plates, Gujarat, AD 595–596
  [66:2:8.3] Bhaskara I's circle for zero | 629 CE
  [66:2:8.4] Gwalior inscription – zero as a circle | 876 CE
[66:2:9] - Zero and decimals reached the **Islamic world and Europe through the Arabs** – zero did not come to India from Europe.
[66:2:10] - Romaka and Paulisa Siddhantas show **Greek** input in Gupta science.
[66:2:11] ~~ Sources: NextGen Indian History APPSC Part 3 p.10 (Brahmagupta gravitation, Aryabhata, Varahamihira and Greek astronomy), p.26 (Siddhanta Shiromani, Panchasiddhantika); app notes 1:66 (sub 4, 5)
## SUB 3 | Kalidasa and the Mahakavyas
[66:3:0] # Kalidasa
[66:3:1] - Greatest Sanskrit poet-dramatist; one of the **Navaratnas of Chandragupta II** (MPPSC 1990) – not Samudragupta, Chandragupta I or Ashoka.
[66:3:2] TABLE head: Type | Works
  [66:3:2.0] Dramas (3) | Abhijnana Shakuntalam (MPPSC 2000), Malavikagnimitram, Vikramorvashiyam
  [66:3:2.1] Mahakavyas | Raghuvamsha (Raghu dynasty), Kumarasambhava (birth of Kumara) (State PSC)
  [66:3:2.2] Lyric poems | Meghaduta, Ritusamhara
[66:3:3] - **Malavikagnimitram**: love of **Agnimitra** (**Shunga king of Vidisha**) and Malavika.

  [66:3:5.2] Shringara Shataka (Shataka-traya) | Bhartrihari (UPPCS 2025)
  [66:3:5.3] Mudrarakshasa | Vishakhadatta
  [66:3:5.4] Kiratarjuniyam | Bharavi
[66:3:6] # The five Mahakavyas

  [66:3:7.2] Shishupalavadha | Magha | Krishna slays Shishupala
  [66:3:7.3] Naishadhiyacharita | Sriharsha (12th c.) | Nala and Damayanti

## SUB 4 | Sculpture and the Mehrauli Iron Pillar
[66:4:0] # Sculpture
[66:4:1] - Gupta stone sculpture grew out of the **Mathura school**; Gupta art showed Vishnu, Shiva and other Hindu gods.
[66:4:2] - **Sarnath school**: polished **Chunar buff sandstone**, little decoration; typical mudra = **Dharmachakra**; the Sarnath **Bhumisparsha mudra** Buddha also belongs to the **Gupta period** (UP UDA/LDA 2010) – not Kushana, Vardhana or Rajput.
[66:4:3] TABLE head: Image | Place | Feature
  [66:4:3.0] Sultanganj Buddha | Bhagalpur, Bihar | Bronze, over 2 m
  [66:4:3.1] Eran Varaha | Eran, MP | Vaishnava presence
[66:4:4] - Apr 2025: the PM gifted a Sarnath-style Buddha in **Dhyan mudra** to the King of Thailand.
[66:4:5] # Mehrauli iron pillar
[66:4:6] - Inscription names the king **"Chandra"** = **Chandragupta II** → a **Gupta** work (SSC 2012; UPPCS 2002) – not Ashoka, Harsha or Anangapal (who later moved it to Delhi).
[66:4:7] - Stands in the courtyard of the **Quwwat-ul-Islam mosque**, Qutb complex; originally at **Udayagiri near Vidisha** (Vishnupadagiri).
[66:4:8] - Studied for its **rustlessness** (CDS 2011) – **high-phosphorus** iron forms a protective film.
[66:4:9] ~~ Sources: NextGen Indian History APPSC Part 3 p.13 (Mehrauli pillar not rusted; Sultanganj; Mathura school; Sarnath Dharmachakra); app notes 1:66 (sub 8)

## SUB 6 | Gupta Coins
[66:6:0] - **Gold = Dinara** (UPPCS 1992); **silver = Rupaka** (UPSC 1997; IAS 1996) – not karshapana, nishka or pana.
[66:6:1] - **Chandragupta I** = first Gupta coin issuer (king-queen type with Kumaradevi).
[66:6:2] - Silver began under **Chandragupta II** after the conquest of the **Western Kshatrapas**, modelled on **Saka** silver issues.
[66:6:3] - Largest hoard: **Bayana (Bharatpur, Rajasthan)**.
[66:6:4] TABLE head: Coin type | Ruler
  [66:6:4.0] King-queen (with Kumaradevi) | Chandragupta I
  [66:6:4.1] Veena-player (lyrist), tiger-slayer, Ashvamedha | Samudragupta
  [66:6:4.2] Archer, lion-slayer, silver | Chandragupta II
  [66:6:4.3] King feeding a peacock (Kartikeya) | Kumaragupta I
  [66:6:4.4] Bow, arrow, Garuda, Lakshmi | Skandagupta
[66:6:5] - The **veena-player** coins reveal the **Guptas'** love of music (SSC 2011).
[66:6:6] ~~ Sources: NextGen Indian History APPSC Part 3 p.4-6, p.16-18 (dinara, rupyaka, coin types); app notes 1:66 (sub 10)
## SUB 7 | Bagh, Udayagiri and Other Cave Sites
[66:7:0] TABLE head: Site | Place | Feature
  [66:7:0.0] Bagh | Dhar district, MP, Vindhya slopes, Baghani river | 9 Buddhist viharas, late 4th–6th c.; Hallisaka painting = a joyous folk dance (UPSC 2026); Cave 4 = Rang Mahal
  [66:7:0.1] Udayagiri | Near Vidisha, MP | 20 caves (19 Hindu, 1 Jain) under Chandragupta II; colossal Varaha panel; Virasena's inscription on his conquests
  [66:7:0.2] Ellora | Aurangabad | Buddhist, Hindu and Jain caves (Rashtrakuta Kailasa)
  [66:7:0.3] Mandapeshwar | Mumbai | Buddhist, later Christian
[66:7:1] - The only two surviving examples of **Gupta-age cave painting** = **Ajanta and Bagh** (UPSC 2010); Bagh paintings follow the Ajanta school with folk themes.
[66:7:2] - **Buddhist caves:** Ajanta, Bagh; **Sanchi** is a Buddhist stupa site; **Bulsar** (Valsad, Gujarat) has **no** Buddhist caves (MPPSC 2022 key).
[66:7:3] - Gupta **Udayagiri (MP)** ≠ Kharavela's Jain Udayagiri (Odisha). Udayagiri is **Hindu** – Ajanta, Bagh and Amaravati are Buddhist.
[66:7:4] - AP angle: **Mogalrajapuram** (Vijayawada) – 5 caves with a **Nataraja**; **Bhairavakonda** – 8 Kapalika caves (Vishnukundin-era rock-cut style).
[66:7:5] ~~ Sources: NextGen Indian History APPSC Part 3 p.19 (Bagh epitomises the Ajanta school); PMF Art & Culture Part 1; app notes 1:66 (sub 9)
## SUB 8 | The Golden Age Label
[66:8:0] - **Gupta** rule is called the **Golden (Classical) Age** of ancient India (UPPCS 2004) – famed for **art and architecture** (SSC 2001), not imperialism or land reform.
[66:8:1] - Peak of **Sanskrit literature**, **mathematics and astronomy**, **Ajanta painting**, **Sarnath sculpture**; shift from **rock-cut to free-standing structural temples**.
[66:8:2] - **Nalanda** drew foreign students; **Balaputradeva of Srivijaya** endowed a monastery there.
[66:8:3] - **Criticism:** spread of **vishti** (forced labour), land grants and feudatories, decline of trade and towns, rigid caste, falling status of women.
[66:8:4] ~~ Sources: NextGen Indian History APPSC Part 3 p.6-8, p.13; app notes 1:66 (sub 0)

## SUB 1 | Hiuen Tsang (Xuanzang) – Journey, Si-Yu-Ki and Observations
[67:1:0] # Profile
[67:1:1] - Chinese Buddhist monk, the "**Prince of Pilgrims**"; visited India in **Harsha's** reign (SSC 2019; UPPCS 2012; State PSC) – **Fa-Hien** came under **Chandragupta II** (so "Fa-Hien under Harsha, Hiuen Tsang under Chandragupta II" are both wrong).
[67:1:2] - Left **Changan** (Tang capital) in **629**; emperor **Taizong** had banned foreign travel, so he went **on his own** by the Silk Route – **no one sent him as an emissary** (UPPCS 2007); back in China in **645**, about **16 years** later.
[67:1:3] - At Harsha's court **631**; studied at **Nalanda** under **Silabhadra** (Yogashastra) and taught there.
[67:1:4] - His record = **Si-Yu-Ki** ("Records of the Western World") (UPPCS 2016) – the main reason he is remembered (RAS 1992). Not Fa-Hien, Al-Biruni or Megasthenes.
[67:1:5] - Praised **Harsha**, **Pulakesin II** and Pallava **Narasimhavarman I**.
[67:1:6] TABLE head: Pilgrim | Period
  [67:1:6.0] Fa-Hien | Chandragupta II
  [67:1:6.1] Hiuen Tsang | Harsha
  [67:1:6.2] I-Tsing | Late 7th c.; came by sea via Srivijaya; studied at Nalanda; records Maharaja Sri Gupta (the first Gupta) building a temple for Chinese pilgrims
[67:1:7] # Observations
[67:1:8] TABLE head: Aspect | Observation
  [67:1:8.0] Law and order | Generally good, but roads were not safe – he was robbed (IAS 2013 statement I false)
  [67:1:8.1] Punishment | Ordeals by water, fire, weighing and poison (statement II true)
  [67:1:8.2] Tax | Light; duties at ferries and barrier stations (statement III true)
  [67:1:8.3] Economy | Trade declining; Mathura famous for cotton cloth; Thanesar prosperous by trade
  [67:1:8.4] Caste, women | Rigid caste, untouchables; position of women declined
  [67:1:8.5] Religion | Buddhism declining, Brahmanism rising; he also records Jain (Nirgrantha) ascetics
[67:1:9] # Places described
[67:1:10] TABLE head: Place | Record
  [67:1:10.0] Bhinmal (Pi-lo-mo-lo) | Gurjara capital (RAS 2007)
  [67:1:10.1] Sun temple of Multan | Also described by Abu Zaid, Al-Masudi, Alberuni; Sambapur pilgrimage = Sun worship (UPPCS 2020: both true)
  [67:1:10.2] Kannauj | Premier city of the north
[67:1:11] ~~ Sources: NextGen Indian History APPSC Part 3 p.18, p.26 (Shi-Yu-Ki; praised Harsha, Narasimhavarman, Pulakesin II; studied at Nalanda); Beal, Si-Yu-Ki (Nirgranthas at Vaishali, Pundravardhana, Samatata); https://www.britannica.com/biography/Xuanzang; app notes 1:67 (sub 9)
## SUB 2 | Harsha – Dynasty, Family, Rivals and Capital
[67:2:0] # Pushyabhuti (Vardhana) dynasty
[67:2:1] - Founded at **Thanesar (Sthanvishvara)** by **Pushyabhuti** per Bana's Harshacharita (State PSC); NextGen names **Naravardhana** as the first historical king.
[67:2:2] - **Prabhakaravardhana** (title Maharajadhiraja), Harsha's father; mother **Yashomati** became sati in 605.
[67:2:3] - Order: **Adityavardhana → Prabhakaravardhana → Rajyavardhana → Harshavardhana**.
[67:2:4] - **Rajyavardhana**, the **elder** brother, was killed by **Shashanka**; Harsha then took the throne (SSC 2019).
[67:2:5] # Family and rivals
[67:2:6] TABLE head: Person | Role
  [67:2:6.0] Grahavarman (Maukhari) | Harsha's brother-in-law, husband of Rajyashri
  [67:2:6.1] Devagupta | Ruler of Malwa who killed Grahavarman and held Rajyashri at Kannauj
  [67:2:6.2] Shashanka (Sasanka) | Ruler of Gauda (Bengal), capital Karnasuvarna; killed Rajyavardhana; cut the Bodhi tree at Gaya; Harsha's Bengal contemporary (RRB 2005)
  [67:2:6.3] Bhaskaravarman | Ruler of Kamarupa, Harsha's friend and ally
  [67:2:6.4] Dhruvasena II | Valabhi (Maitraka); defeated, made vassal, married Harsha's daughter
  [67:2:6.5] Pulakesin II | Badami Chalukya; defeated Harsha on the Narmada, took the title Paramesvara
[67:2:7] - SI 2023 match: **Devagupta – Malwa (killed the brother-in-law)**, **Sasanka – Gauda (killed the brother)**, **Bhaskaravarman – Kamarupa friend**, **Grahavarman – brother-in-law**.
[67:2:8] # Capital, titles, dates
[67:2:9] - Capital moved from **Thanesar to Kannauj** (UPPCS 1992; AP Sachivalayam) – Kannauj became the capital of his empire (UPPCS 1993), not Prayaga, Pataliputra or Delhi.
[67:2:10] - Titles: **Siladitya** (APPSC G1), **Sakalottarapathanatha** (lord of all North India).
[67:2:11] TABLE head: Year | Event
  [67:2:11.0] 606 | Accession at 16; Harsha era begins
  [67:2:11.1] c. 618–619 (NextGen: 637) | Defeat by Pulakesin II on the Narmada (Aihole inscription, 634)
  [67:2:11.2] 631 | Hiuen Tsang at court
  [67:2:11.3] 643 | Kannauj assembly
  [67:2:11.4] 647 | Death without heir
[67:2:12] ~~ Sources: NextGen Indian History APPSC Part 3 p.16-18 (family, Sasanka, Devagupta, Pulakesin II, Kannauj capital, Siladitya); app notes 1:67 (sub 1-3)
## SUB 3 | Vakatakas
[67:3:0] - Rose in the **Deccan** after the weakening of the **Satavahanas**; founder **Vindhyashakti** (3rd c.); **Pravarasena I** was his **son** (CGPSC 2021: only statement (i) true).
[67:3:1] - Order: **Satavahanas → Vakatakas → Chalukyas** (JPSC 2021).

  [67:3:2.0] Vindhyashakti | Founder
  [67:3:2.1] Pravarasena I | Real founder of Vakataka power; only Vakataka Samrat (SI 2018); four Ashvamedhas (UPPCS 2003), Vajapeya; empire Bundelkhand to the Deccan; in the Puranas
  [67:3:2.2] Rudrasena II | Married Prabhavatigupta
  [67:3:2.3] Prabhavatigupta | Daughter of Chandragupta II; regent → Gupta indirect control of the Deccan
  [67:3:2.4] Pravarasena II | Prakrit Setubandha
  [67:3:2.5] Harishena (Vatsagulma branch) | Ajanta Caves 16 and 17 through minister Varahadeva

## SUB 4 | Post-Gupta Kingdoms – Maukharis and Maitrakas
[67:4:0] - **Maukharis**: Gupta feudatories from **Gaya**; capital **Kannauj** (CGPSC 2011) – Thanesar was the Pushyabhuti capital, Purushapura the Kushana.
[67:4:1] - **Maitrakas** of **Valabhi** ruled **Gujarat and Saurashtra** after the Guptas (APPSC ASO).
[67:4:2] - Later Guptas in Magadha; Pushyabhutis of Thanesar moved to Kannauj.
[67:4:3] - **Hundi** in post-Harsha sources = a **bill of exchange** (UPSC 2020).
[67:4:4] ~~ Sources: NextGen Indian History APPSC Part 3 p.6 (Later Guptas, Maukharis, Maitrakas, Pushyabhutis); app notes 1:67 (sub 1)

[67:7:2] - Officials paid by **land grants** → feudal trend; samantas sent tribute.

  [67:7:3.3] Skandagupta | Elephant force
[67:7:4] - Punishments: **four ordeals – water, fire, weighing, poison**; prisoners kept in dungeons.

## SUB 0 | Mahaviharas – Founder and Location
[69:0:0] # The five great monasteries
[69:0:1] TABLE head: Mahavihara | Founder | Present location
  [69:0:1.0] Nalanda | Kumaragupta I (Gupta, 5th c. AD) | Nalanda, Bihar (ancient Magadha); Pala patronage, revived by Dharmapala
  [69:0:1.1] Odantapuri (Uddandapura, Udantpur) | Gopala | Bihar Sharif, Bihar; model for Tibetan monasteries
  [69:0:1.2] Vikramashila | Dharmapala | Antichak, Bhagalpur district, Bihar, on the Ganga
  [69:0:1.3] Somapura | Dharmapala | Paharpur, Naogaon, Bangladesh
  [69:0:1.4] Jagaddala | Ramapala | Varendra, Naogaon, Bangladesh
[69:0:2] - **Vikramashila = Dharmapala:** asked 10 times (UPPSC 2002, 2008, 2016; UPRO 2017, 2018; Uttarakhand 2024; APPSC G1) – not Gopala, Devapala, Mahipala, Ramapala, Kumaragupta I, Harsha or Lakshmanasena.
[69:0:3] - **Odantapuri = Gopala** (APPSC) – in **Bihar** (State PSC).
[69:0:4] - **Somapura = Dharmapala** (UPPSC 1999).
[69:0:5] - **Nalanda = Kumaragupta I, Gupta dynasty** (APPSC G1; State PSC) – not a Pala foundation; the **oldest** of these (RAS 1992).
[69:0:6]   - **⚠ Disputed:** "most ancient monastery" keys give **Nalanda**; strictly the Bhaja rock-cut vihara (2nd c. BCE) is older.
[69:0:7] - Together = **Panchamahavihara** (Tibetan sources).
[69:0:8] - **Vikramashila:** centre of **Tantric / Vajrayana** Buddhism and logic; ~3,000 scholars, six colleges, *dvarapandita* gatekeepers; trained monks for Tibet. **Jagaddala** translated books into **Tibetan**.
[69:0:9] - **Destruction:** by **Bakhtiyar Khilji**, c. **1193–1200** (1194 for Nalanda in one tradition); Jagaddala sacked in the early **13th** c.
[69:0:10] - **Nava Nalanda Mahavihara:** a **Pali research centre** founded by **Bhikshu Jagadish Kashyap**; foundation stone **20 November 1951** (State PSC).
[69:0:11] - **⚠ Trap:** Vikramashila is in **Bhagalpur** (not Banka).
[69:0:12] ~~ Sources: NextGen Rocket Indian History Part 1 p.60; PMF Ancient & Medieval Part 3 p.141-144; app notes 1:69 (sub 2)
## SUB 1 | Odd One Out – Centres of Learning
[69:1:0] - **Early medieval (Pala) centres:** Nalanda, Vikramashila, **Odantapuri (Uddandapur)**, Somapura.
[69:1:1] - **Taxila = odd one out** (Uttarakhand 2016): early Buddhist centre, capital of **Gandhara** (Rawalpindi district, Pakistan); students – Chanakya, Chandragupta Maurya, **Charaka**, Jivaka.
[69:1:2] - **Valabhi:** **Hinayana** centre of Harsha's time (Maitrakas, Gujarat) – not a Pala mahavihara.
[69:1:3] ~~ Sources: NextGen Rocket Indian History Part 1 p.60; app notes 1:69 (sub 3)
## SUB 2 | Gopala and the Pala Rulers
[69:2:0] # Gopala – the founder
[69:2:1] - **Founder of the Pala dynasty:** **Gopala** (UPPSC 2015) – not Dharmapala, Devapala or Ramapala.
[69:2:2] - **Elected** by the chiefs (c. 750) to end **matsyanyaya** (anarchy, law of the jungle); born near **Pundravardhana** (per Taranatha).
[69:2:3] - **Source:** the **Khalimpur inscription of Dharmapala** records his election.
[69:2:4] - Replaced the later Guptas of Magadha and the **Khadgas** of **eastern Bengal**; built **Odantapuri**.
[69:2:5] - **Kings chosen by the people:** **Gopala** and **Nandivarman II Pallavamalla**.
[69:2:6] # Later Palas
[69:2:7] TABLE head: Ruler | Achievement
  [69:2:7.0] Dharmapala (770–810) | Founded Vikramashila and Somapura; installed Chakrayudha at Kannauj; defeated by Dhruva and by Nagabhata II near Monghyr
  [69:2:7.1] Devapala (810–850) | Granted five villages for Balaputradeva's Nalanda monastery (Nalanda copper plate); beat Amoghavarsha and Mihira Bhoja
  [69:2:7.2] Mahipala I | Revived Pala power; defeated by Rajendra Chola (c. 1023)
  [69:2:7.3] Ramapala (c. 1072–1126) | Last strong ruler; Kaivarta revolt; founded Jagaddala
[69:2:8] - Palas = **last great royal patrons of Buddhism** (Mahayana, Vajrayana) in India; took it to Tibet and SE Asia.
[69:2:9] ~~ Sources: PMF Ancient & Medieval Part 3 p.141-144; app notes 1:69 (sub 0, 1)
## SUB 3 | Acharyas, Tibet and Southeast Asia
[69:3:0] # Acharyas
[69:3:1] TABLE head: Acharya | Institution | Note
  [69:3:1.0] Shilabhadra | Nalanda | Head in Harsha's time
  [69:3:1.1] Shantarakshita | Nalanda | Founded Samye monastery in Tibet
  [69:3:1.2] Atisha Dipankara Srijnana | Vikramashila | Went to Tibet in the 11th c., revived Buddhism (APPSC G1)
  [69:3:1.3] Sakya Sri Bhadra | Jagaddala | Took Tantric Buddhism to Tibet
[69:3:2] - **Kautilya** was NOT a mahavihara acharya; Nagarjuna, Vasubandhu are earlier; Pujyapada was a Jain grammarian.
[69:3:3] - **AP angle:** Andhra's **Dharmakirti** taught at Nalanda; studied under **Dharmapala of Kanchi**, head of Nalanda (not the Pala king).
[69:3:4] # Southeast Asia
[69:3:5] - **Balaputradeva:** **Shailendra** ruler of **Suvarnadvipa / Suvarnabhumi** (Sumatra–Java); built a monastery at Nalanda; his envoy obtained **five villages** from **Devapala** (BPSC 2018; State PSC) – not Dharmapala.
[69:3:6] ~~ Sources: PMF Ancient & Medieval Part 3 p.143-145; app notes 1:69 (sub 4, 5)
## SUB 4 | Sena Successors and the Lakshmana Era
[69:4:0] TABLE head: Ruler | Fact
  [69:4:0.0] Samantasena | Founder; from Karnataka; Pala feudatory in Rarh
  [69:4:0.1] Vijayasena | Founded independent Sena rule; expelled the last Pala Madanapala
  [69:4:0.2] Ballalasena | Scholar king (Danasagara, Adbhutasagara)
  [69:4:0.3] Lakshmanasena | Last great Sena; court poet Jayadeva; ousted by Bakhtiyar Khilji (Nadia)
[69:4:1] - **New Samvat:** **Lakshmana Samvat** (Lakshmana era, from c. **1119** AD) = **Lakshmanasena**, **Sena** dynasty (UPPSC 1999, 2005) – not Dharmapala, Devapala or the Palas.
[69:4:2] ~~ Sources: PMF Ancient & Medieval Part 3 p.144; https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lakshmana_Sena; app notes 1:69 (sub 7)

=== NOTES 1:73 | Badami (vatapi) Chalukyas – Pulakesin I, Pulakesin Ii, Aihole Inscription of Ravikirti
## SUB 0 | Dynasty, Capital and Mother Goddess
[73:0:0] - **Badami (Vatapi) Chalukyas:** **c. 543–753 CE**; ruled the **Deccan and the South**, **NOT North India** (Uttarakhand 2010: "dynasty that did not rule North India" = Chalukyas).
[73:0:1] - **Capital = Vatapi** (UPPSC 1991 ×2) = modern **Badami, Bagalkot district, Karnataka** – not Shravasti, **Kanchi** (Pallava) or Kannauj; sandstone hills around Agastya lake. Before Vatapi, **Aihole (Ayyavole)** was the seat.
[73:0:2] - **Vatapi fortified by Pulakesin I** – **Badami cliff inscription, 543 CE**.
[73:0:3] - **Mother goddess:** the early Chalukyas called themselves **Hariti-putras** and worshipped **Hariti** (G2 Mains 2019; APPSC PYQ) – not Kushmandini, Padmakshi or Kanakadurga.
[73:0:4] ~~ Sources: NextGen Rocket Indian History Part 2 p.121-122; NextGen AP History Part 7 p.1; PMF Ancient & Medieval Part 3 p.107; app notes 1:73 (sub 0)
## SUB 1 | Pulakesin II – the Greatest Chalukya
[73:1:0] # Greatest ruler
[73:1:1] - **Pulakesin II (610–642)** = the greatest ruler of the **Chalukyas of Vatapi** (UPPSC 1991; SSC 2013) – not Kalyani Chalukyas, Pallavas or Cholas; not Vikramaditya, Mangalesha or Pulakesin I.
[73:1:2] - **Hiuen Tsang** visited his kingdom and praised him (APPSC FRO 2012) – not Pulakesin I or III; Madhava Varma was a Vishnukundin.
[73:1:3] # Events
[73:1:4] TABLE head: Year (CE) | Event
  [73:1:4.0] 617 | Satara inscription: brother Kubja Vishnuvardhana viceroy of Vengi
  [73:1:4.1] 618–19 | Stopped Harsha on the Narmada
  [73:1:4.2] 624 | Vengi independent = Eastern Chalukyas (capital Pithapuram)
  [73:1:4.3] c. 626 | Embassy with Persian king Khusrau II
  [73:1:4.4] 634–35 | Aihole inscription
  [73:1:4.5] 642 | Pallava Narasimhavarman I destroyed Vatapi → title Vatapikonda
[73:1:5] - **Eastern campaign:** **Kosala & Kalinga** → Vengi → defeated the **Durjayas** → then the Pallava **Mahendravarman I**.
[73:1:6] # Titles and foreign accounts
[73:1:7] TABLE head: Ruler | Title
  [73:1:7.0] Kushanas | Devaputra
  [73:1:7.1] Pulakesin II | Dakshinapatheshwara
  [73:1:7.2] Harshavardhana | Sakalottarapathanatha
  [73:1:7.3] Samudragupta | Kaviraja
[73:1:8] - Match (UPRO 2023): **A-i, B-iii, C-ii, D-iv**.
[73:1:9] - **Paramesvara** after beating **Harsha**; also Satyashraya, Prithvivallabha.
[73:1:10] - China–India relations under the Chalukyas: **Ma Twan-lin** (Matwalin). **Lohnara inscription (630 CE)** does NOT list Harsha; Aihole does.
[73:1:11] - First **gold coins** of South India credited to Pulakesin II.
[73:1:12] ~~ Sources: NextGen Rocket Indian History Part 2 p.121-122; PMF Ancient & Medieval Part 3 p.107-108; app notes 1:73 (sub 3)
## SUB 2 | Aihole Inscription of Ravikirti
[73:2:0] TABLE head: Point | Fact
  [73:2:0.0] Author | Ravikirti, Jain court poet of Pulakesin II
  [73:2:0.1] Language / script | Sanskrit prasasti, Southern Brahmi
  [73:2:0.2] Date | 634–35 CE (Saka era)
  [73:2:0.3] Place | Meguti Jain temple, Aihole
  [73:2:0.4] Poets named | Kalidasa and Bharavi (Ravikirti claimed fame like theirs)
[73:2:1] - **Kalidasa is mentioned in** the **Aihole inscription of Pulakesin II** (IAS 1994; UPPSC 2013) – not the Allahabad pillar, Alapadu grant, Hanumakonda, Gwalior, Karamdanda or Mathura pillar inscriptions.
[73:2:2] - **Victories:** **Harsha** (Narmada), **Kadambas** (Banavasi), Gangas, Alupas, Mauryas of Konkan, Latas, Malavas, Gurjaras, **Kosala, Kalinga, Pishtapura** (**Pithapuram**), **Pallavas**.
[73:2:3] - Kirtivarman I = "**night of doom**" to the **Nalas, Mauryas and Kadambas**.
[73:2:4] ~~ Sources: NextGen Rocket Indian History Part 1 p.11; NextGen Rocket Indian History Part 2 p.121; app notes 1:73 (sub 4)
## SUB 3 | Andhra Inscriptions and Place Names
[73:3:0] TABLE head: Inscription | Event / name
  [73:3:0.0] Marturu (Maruturu) | Calls Mangalagiri "Mangalapura"
  [73:3:0.1] Maruturu and Kopparam | Defeated Mahendravarman I; won the land between the Krishna and Godavari
  [73:3:0.2] Kopparam | Names Kubja Vishnuvardhana as Pulakesin II's representative
  [73:3:0.3] Kubja Vishnuvardhana | Chipurupalli, Kopparam, Chejarala, Timmapuram
  [73:3:0.4] Pune plates (669), Vishnuvardhana II | First reference to Guntur as Kumturu

## SUB 4 | Rulers and Succession
[73:4:0] TABLE head: Ruler | Reign | Key fact
  [73:4:0.0] Pulakesin I | 543–566 | Real founder; Ashvamedha; walled Vatapi
  [73:4:0.1] Kirtivarman I | 566–597 | Took Kadambas, Gangas, Mauryas of Konkan; Bahusuvarna-Agnishtoma (Mahakuta pillar)
  [73:4:0.2] Mangalesha | 597–609 | Regent; earliest rock-cut caves at Badami
  [73:4:0.3] Pulakesin II | 610–642 | Zenith
  [73:4:0.4] Vikramaditya I | 655–680 | Revived power after the Pallava occupation of Vatapi
  [73:4:0.5] Vikramaditya II | 733–746 | Took Kanchi thrice but spared it; queen Lokamahadevi built the Virupaksha temple, Pattadakal
  [73:4:0.6] Kirtivarman II | 746–753 | Last; overthrown by Rashtrakuta Dantidurga
[73:4:1] - Other sacrifices: **Vajapeya, Hiranyagarbha** – claim to **Kshatriya** status.
[73:4:2] - **Succession war:** Kirtivarman I left minor sons → brother **Mangalesha** ruled as **regent**; Pulakesin II killed him at **Elapattu-Simbige** (Bana territory, c. 609–10).
[73:4:3] ~~ Sources: NextGen Rocket Indian History Part 2 p.121; PMF Ancient & Medieval Part 3 p.107-108; app notes 1:73 (sub 1, 2)

=== NOTES 1:77 | Pallava Art and Architecture – Mandagapattu Inscription, Mahabalipuram Rathas, Shore Temple, Kailasanatha
## SUB 0 | Mahabalipuram – Rathas, Reliefs and the Shore Temple
[77:0:0] # Pancha (Pandava) Rathas
[77:0:1] - **Builder:** the **Pallavas** under **Narasimhavarman I (Mamalla, 630–668)** – "Seven Ratha" / Pancha Ratha temples (APPSC GS 2025; UPPSC 1994, 2014, 2015; SSC 2008, CGL 2020) – not Mahendravarman, Paramesvaravarman, Nandivarman, Simhavarman, Pulakesin II or Mayuravarman; not Cholas, Cheras, Chedis, Chalukyas, Rashtrakutas or Satavahanas.
[77:0:2] - **Monolithic:** each carved from **one granite rock**, copying wooden and structural forms (not brick and timber).
[77:0:3] - **Five:** **Dharmaraja, Bhima, Arjuna, Nakula-Sahadeva, Draupadi**.
[77:0:4] TABLE head: Ratha | Special fact
  [77:0:4.0] Dharmaraja | Largest; forerunner of the Dravida vimana
  [77:0:4.1] Draupadi | Smallest (UPPSC Mains 2011); hut-shaped single cell, no ornament
  [77:0:4.2] Nakula-Sahadeva | Apsidal
[77:0:5] # Reliefs and mandapas
[77:0:6] TABLE head: Monument | Theme
  [77:0:6.0] Arjuna's Penance / Descent of the Ganga | Bhagiratha's penance; largest open-air rock relief in India – the "descent of the Ganga" relief is at Mahabalipuram (Asst. Comm. 2018), not Ellora, Sanchi or Amaravati
  [77:0:6.1] Varaha Mandapa | Varaha rescuing Bhudevi
  [77:0:6.2] Mahishasuramardini Cave | Durga slaying Mahishasura
  [77:0:6.3] Krishna Mandapa | Krishna lifting Govardhana
[77:0:7] - Pancha Rathas, Varaha Mandapa and Mahishasuramardini cave = **Narasimhavarman I** phase.
[77:0:8] # Shore Temple
[77:0:9] - **Structural** temple of **Narasimhavarman II (Rajasimha)**; **two Shiva shrines + one Vishnu shrine**; sole survivor of the "**Seven Pagodas**".
[77:0:10] # Port and UNESCO
[77:0:11] - **Mahabalipuram = the famous Pallava port** (APSLPRB SI 2019) – not Krishnapatnam, Motupalli (Kakatiya) or Achalapuram.
[77:0:12] TABLE head: Point | Mahabalipuram | Ajanta
  [77:0:12.0] UNESCO | 1984 | 1983
  [77:0:12.1] Patron | Hindu; Pallavas | Buddhist; Satavahana and Vakataka phases
  [77:0:12.2] Form | Rathas, reliefs, Shore Temple | 25 viharas + 4 chaityas; found 1819 by John Smith
[77:0:13] ~~ Sources: PMF Art & Culture (src/indian-history/pmf-art-culture-03.pdf) p.46-47; PMF Art & Culture (pmf-art-culture-01.pdf) Pallava section; PMF Ancient & Medieval p.115; app notes 1:77 (sub 2, 4)
## SUB 1 | Phases of Pallava Architecture, Mandagapattu and Painting
[77:1:0] # Four phases
[77:1:1] TABLE head: Phase | Ruler | Type | Examples
  [77:1:1.0] Mahendra | Mahendravarman I (600–630) | Rock-cut pillared mandapas | Mandagapattu, Mahendravadi, Dalavanur
  [77:1:1.1] Mamalla | Narasimhavarman I (630–668) | Monolithic rathas and mandapas | Pancha Rathas
  [77:1:1.2] Rajasimha | Narasimhavarman II | First structural temples | Shore Temple; Kailasanatha, Kanchi
  [77:1:1.3] Nandivarman / Aparajita | Nandivarman II and later | Smaller structural temples | Vaikuntha Perumal
[77:1:2] - Evolution: **rock-cut → monolithic → structural**.
[77:1:3] # Mandagapattu inscription
[77:1:4] - Issued by **Mahendravarman I**: a temple for **Brahma, Vishnu and Shiva** made **without brick, timber, metal or mortar** (stone is not in the list).
[77:1:5] - = **first rock-cut temple in South India**; first **dvarapalakas** at a temple entrance.
[77:1:6] # Painting
[77:1:7] - **Sittannavasal** (**Pudukkottai**, TN): **Jain** cave with **lotus-pond** murals; renovated by the **Pandyas** (9th c.).
[77:1:8] - **Panamalai** painting of **Parvati** = **Rajasimha** period.
[77:1:9] # Builder match
[77:1:10] - **Shore Temple – Narasimhavarman II; Brihadisvara – Rajaraja Chola I; Gommateshwara – Chamundaraya; Barabar caves – Ashoka**.
[77:1:11] ~~ Sources: PMF Art & Culture (src/indian-history/pmf-art-culture-01.pdf) Pallava architecture; app notes 1:77 (sub 0, 1, 5, 7)
## SUB 2 | Kanchi Temples – Kailasanatha and Vaikuntha Perumal
[77:2:0] - **Kailasanatha (Rajasimheshvara), Kanchi: built by Narasimhavarman II (Rajasimha)** (G2 2000 ×2) – not Mahendravarman I, Narasimhavarman I or Nandivarman Pallavamalla; **completed by Mahendravarman III**.
[77:2:1]   - **Sandstone**; the **oldest surviving Pallava structural temple** at Kanchi; carries **Vikramaditya II's Kannada inscription**; model for the **Virupaksha, Pattadakal**.
[77:2:2] - **Vaikuntha Perumal, Kanchi:** **Nandivarman II**; **Vishnu**; storeyed sanctum and panels on Pallava history.
[77:2:3] ~~ Sources: PMF Ancient & Medieval (src/indian-history/pmf-ancient-medieval-03.pdf) p.115; PMF Art & Culture (pmf-art-culture-01.pdf) Pallava section; app notes 1:77 (sub 3)
## SUB 3 | Pallava-style Rock-cut Caves in Andhra – Bhairavakona and Undavalli
[77:3:0] - **Bhairavakona = a centre of Shaivism** (G2 2008; APPSC PYQ) – not Buddhism, Jainism or Vaishnavism; **eight** rock-cut Shiva caves resembling early Pallava caves.
[77:3:1]   - Location: Nallamala hills, **Prakasam district** on the Nellore border (old books and keys: "Nellore district").
[77:3:2] TABLE head: Cave | Location | Attribution
  [77:3:2.0] Undavalli | Guntur, Krishna bank | Vishnukundins – not Cholas; reclining Anantasayana Vishnu
  [77:3:2.1] Mogalrajapuram | Vijayawada | Vishnukundins; Shiva and Vishnu shrines
  [77:3:2.2] Bhairavakona | Prakasam | Vishnukundin / early Pallava idiom
[77:3:3] - The **Vishnukundins** started Hindu cave temples in Telugu lands, imitating the **Pallava** cave style.
[77:3:4] ~~ Sources: NextGen AP History (src/ap-history/ap-history-appsc-05.pdf) p.2; NextGen Vishnukundins p.9, p.12; Rocket AP History p.8; NextGen AP History Previous Papers p.28; app notes 1:77 (sub 6)

=== NOTES 1:78 | Eastern Chalukyas of Vengi – Kubja Vishnuvardhana, Dynastic History, Patronage of Telugu (nannaya)
## SUB 0 | Gunaga Vijayaditya III (848–892) – Greatest King, Titles, Pandaranga, Kandukuru
[78:0:0] # The greatest Eastern Chalukya king
[78:0:1] - **Gunaga Vijayaditya = Vijayaditya III**, the **greatest king** of the Vengi Chalukyas (G2 2011 ×2) – not Danarnava, Chalukya Bhima I or Rajaraja Narendra; ruled **43 years**; "Gunaga" for his skill in mathematics.
[78:0:2] - **Military:** defeated the **Rashtrakuta Krishna II** and the **Kalinga king Devendravarma**; expanded the kingdom; issued grand **copper-plate** records with royal titles (ATWO).
[78:0:3] # Titles
[78:0:4] - **Tripura Martya Maheswara** (G2 2012, Mains 2017; G1, G2 PYQ) – not Vishnuvardhana I/III, Vijayaditya I, Kubja Vishnuvardhana, Rajaraja Narendra or Vijayaditya II.
[78:0:5]   - Assumed to commemorate his victory over **Nellore, Kiranapura and Achalapura** (G2 2012).
[78:0:6]   - **⚠ Settled:** the printed key "Kiranapuram, Achalapuram and **Kandukur**" is wrong – NextGen and Rocket give **Nellore, Kiranapura and Achalapura**.
[78:0:7] - Other titles: **Gunaka-Nallata, Parachakra Rama, Vallabha**, Vira Makaradhwaja, Ranaranga Sudraka, Dakshinadhipati (Sachivalayam: the set = **Vijayaditya III**, not Chalukya Bhima, Vishnuvardhana IV or Amoghavarsha).
[78:0:8] # Pandaranga (Panduranga), his commander
[78:0:9] - **Pandaranga = commander of Gunaga Vijayaditya** (G1 1983-84, 1987; Welfare Officers 2017; APPSC PYQ) – i.e. of the **Vengi (Eastern) Chalukyas**, not the Ananda Gotrikas, Pallavas or Badami Chalukyas.
[78:0:10] - One of **four Brahmin generals** (Pandaranga, Vinayaditya Sarma, Kadiyaraju, Rajaditya); subdued the **Boyas**, built **Pandurangapuram** and a Maheswara temple on **Pulicat lake**.
[78:0:11] - Issued the **Addanki inscription** – the **first Telugu verse (padya) inscription**, in **Taruvoja** metre.
[78:0:12] # Kandukuru "on the lines of Bezawada"
[78:0:13] - **Vijayaditya III (Gunaga Vijayaditya)** developed **Kandukuru** like **Bezawada** (G2 2008 ×2, 2019; Mains; APPSC PYQ) – Pandaranga made it a strong fort after conquering the Boya kingdoms.
[78:0:14]   - **⚠ Settled:** one G2 2008 printed key gave **Vijayaditya II** – wrong; Vijayaditya II is the 108-temples king.
[78:0:15] ~~ Sources: NextGen Eastern Chalukyas (src/ap-history/nextgen-06-eastern-chalukyas.pdf) p.2-3, p.7, p.13, p.34; NextGen AP History Previous Papers (src/ap-history/nextgen-previous-papers.txt) p.14, p.19, p.27; Rocket AP History p.47; app notes 1:78 (sub 2)
## SUB 1 | Nannaya and Telugu – Nandampudi, Narayana Bhattu and the First Telugu Inscriptions
[78:1:0] # Nannaya
[78:1:1] - **Nannaya Bhattu** (Adi Kavi), **court poet of Rajaraja Narendra** (G2 1993, 2011 ×2) – Rajaraja Narendra **patronised** him, not Bhima II, Vijayaditya, Vishnuvardhana or Ammaraja; Pampa and Nannechoda are distractors.
[78:1:2] - Began the **Andhra Mahabharatamu** (c. 1045–65; **Adi, Sabha** and part of **Aranya** parvas) – the **earliest surviving Telugu literary work**, in **Champu** (verse + prose) style; the court poet, **not the king**, began it.
[78:1:3] - **Telugu literature owes its origin to the (Eastern) Chalukyas** (APPSC JA) – not Cholas, Cheras or Pandyas; the Vengi court turned Telugu into a literary language.
[78:1:4] - Titles: **Adikavi, Vagadheeshwara, Shabda Shasanudu**; grammar **Andhra Shabda Chintamani**.
[78:1:5] - **A–R (ATWO):** A (earliest surviving Telugu work) and R (translated in the 11th century at Rajaraja Narendra's request) are both true; the key takes R as the explanation of A.
[78:1:6] # Narayana Bhattu and the Nandampudi grant
[78:1:7] - **Narayana Bhattu helped Nannaya** (JA 2012); he was a scholar sent to Vengi as the **Kalyani Chalukya** (Someshvara I) representative; title **Ashtabhasha Kavisekhara**.
[78:1:8] - **Evidence: the Nandampudi grant (copper-plate inscription) of Rajaraja Narendra** (G2 Prelims 2019; Mains 2017; G2 PYQ; APPSC PYQ ×2) – not Andhra Kavi Tarangini, Kollipaka, Pedda Cherukuru, Maruturu, Kupama or Mangallu.
[78:1:9] - **Donee of Nandampudi village = Narayana Bhattu** (G2 Mains 2017; G2 PYQ); **Nannaya composed** the grant – Nannaya, Jina Vallabha and Pavuluri Mallana were not the donee.
[78:1:10] - **Korumelli** plates of Rajaraja Narendra – same scribe as Nandampudi.
[78:1:11] TABLE head: Person | Work / title
  [78:1:11.0] Pavuluri Mallana | Pavuluri Ganitamu – Telugu verse of Mahaviracharya's Ganitasarasangraham; first scientific text in Telugu
  [78:1:11.1] Vemulavada Bhimakavi | Kavijanasrayam
[78:1:12] # First Telugu inscriptions
[78:1:13] TABLE head: Inscription | Issued by | Point
  [78:1:13.0] Kalamalla (c. 575) | Renati Choda Dhananjaya | Earliest Telugu inscription (pre-Nannaya)
  [78:1:13.1] Vipparla (Guntur) | Jayasimha Vallabha I | First (complete) Telugu inscription of the Eastern Chalukyas (G2 2017; Welfare Officers; APPSC PYQ) – not Kubja, Dhananjaya, Shakti Varma, Vishnuvardhana II/III or Vijayaditya
  [78:1:13.2] Addanki | Pandaranga (Gunaga Vijayaditya) | First Telugu verse, Taruvoja metre (APPSC PYQ) – not Attili, Mushinikonda or Kaluchumbarru
  [78:1:13.3] Sataluru | Gunaga Vijayaditya | Champakamala verse; half Telugu, half Sanskrit
  [78:1:13.4] Bezawada | Yuddhamalla II | First Madhyakkara verse; Nagamalleswara temple
  [78:1:13.5] Magallu | Danarnava | First mention of the Kakatiyas (not the Gajapatis)
  [78:1:13.6] Porumamilla | Prince Bhaskara Bhavadura | 12 rules for tank construction
[78:1:14] ~~ Sources: NextGen Eastern Chalukyas (src/ap-history/nextgen-06-eastern-chalukyas.pdf) p.1, p.10, p.20-21, p.30, p.32-33; Rocket Indian History sheet #145 (rocket-indian-history-02.pdf) p.123; app notes 1:78 (sub 6, 8)
## SUB 2 | Capitals and Cities – Rajamahendravaram, Vengi, Pithapuram, Bezawada
[78:2:0] # Rajamahendravaram (Rajahmundry)
[78:2:1] - **Built by Ammaraja I (Vishnuvardhana VI, 921–927)**, title **Rajamahendra**, after which the city is named (APPSC PYQ ×3; JA 2012; G2 2008); he shifted the capital from Vengi there – "**cultural capital of the Andhras**".
[78:2:2]   - **⚠ Settled:** one G2 2008 printed key gave **Rajaraja Narendra** – he only **ruled from** Rajahmundry and **made it famous**; NextGen and its previous-paper key: "**Ammaraja ruler built Rajahmundry**".
[78:2:3] - **Dynasty:** Rajamahendri was built in the time of the **Eastern Chalukyas** (G2 2001, 2002; unknown 2002 "founded by the Eastern Chalukyas") – not Vishnukundins, Kalingas or Vijayanagara.
[78:2:4] - **Statement (VRO):** A – Rajamahendravaram built by **Ammaraja Vishnuvardhana I** ✓; B – **Rajahmundry district** created in the **Madras Presidency in 1823** ✓ (split into Godavari and Krishna in 1859).
[78:2:5] # Capitals in order
[78:2:6] TABLE head: Order | Capital | Ruler linked
  [78:2:6.0] 1 | Pithapuram (Pishtapura) | Kubja Vishnuvardhana
  [78:2:6.1] 2 | Vengi (Pedavegi, near Eluru) | Jayasimha Vallabha I shifted it
  [78:2:6.2] 3 | Rajamahendravaram | Ammaraja I made it capital; Rajaraja Narendra ruled from it
[78:2:7] # Bezawada (Vijayawada)
[78:2:8] - **Kartikeya (Kumaraswamy) temple at Bezawada: Yuddhamalla** (APPSC PYQ), recorded in his **Bezawada inscription**.
[78:2:9] - **Bezawada inscription = Yuddhamalla's reign** (G1 PYQ, stem dates it "885"); it is the famous Telugu **Madhyakkara** verse record of **Yuddhamalla II**, son of Talapa, ruling from **Chebrolu** – the stem's year is loose (Yuddhamalla II is 10th c.).
[78:2:10] - **Vijayawada** took its name from **Vijayaditya** (NextGen: Vijayaditya II); NextGen also says "Vijayawada built by Yuddhamalla".
[78:2:11] # Other names
[78:2:12] TABLE head: Old name | Place
  [78:2:12.0] Andhra Nagaram | Vengi (Dandin's Dashakumaracharita)
  [78:2:12.1] Mangalapura | Mangalagiri (Kopparam / Marturu records)
  [78:2:12.2] Venginadu | Krishna-Godavari doab – core territory

## SUB 3 | Temples, Religion and Jain Patronage
[78:3:0] # Builders
[78:3:1] TABLE head: Temple | Builder
  [78:3:1.0] Kunti Madhava (Vishnu), Pithapuram | Kubja Vishnuvardhana (Welfare Officers 2017 ×2) – not Jayasimha, Mangi Yuvaraja or Vijayaditya
  [78:3:1.1] 108 Shiva temples (Narendreswara) | Vijayaditya II
  [78:3:1.2] Bikkavolu – Mukteshwara, Vijayeshwara, Chandrashekhara, Golingeswara | Gunaga Vijayaditya III
  [78:3:1.3] Pancharamas (Draksharama = Bhimarama, Kumararama, Somarama, Ksheerarama, Amararama); Bhimeswara (Draksharama, Samalkot) | Chalukya Bhima I
  [78:3:1.4] Kartikeya, Bezawada | Yuddhamalla
  [78:3:1.5] Three Shiva temples at Kalidindi for fallen Chola soldiers | Rajaraja Narendra
[78:3:2] - **Vengi school:** Vesara/Chalukya idiom; **local sandstone (not granite)**, raised jagati; leads into the **Chalukya-Chola** style.
[78:3:3] - **Match (APPSC JA):** Bhima – **Draksharama**; Eastern Chalukyas – **Pancharama kshetras**; Rajaraja Narendra – **Chalukya-Chola architecture**; Kakatiyas – **Shaivism almost destroyed Jainism** = A-3, B-4, C-2, D-1.
[78:3:4] # Religion
[78:3:5] - **Shaivism dominant** (Kapalika, Kalamukha, Pasupata sects); mother goddess **Hariti**; tolerant of Jainism and Buddhism.
[78:3:6] # Jain patronage
[78:3:7] - **Ayyana Mahadevi**, queen of **Kubja Vishnuvardhana**, built the Jain **Nedumba (Nadumbi) Vasati / Nedumbasadi** at **Vijayawada** (G2 PYQ; APPSC PYQ) – recorded in the **Musinikonda grant**; not Mylama, Upasika Bodhisiri or Devi Naganika; not Gunaga Vijayaditya, Jatachoda Bhima or Jayasimha Vallabha.
[78:3:8] - **Vimaladitya** = the Eastern Chalukya king who **embraced Jainism** (guru **Trikalayogi Siddhanti**; Ramatirtha cave) (JA 2012) – not Gunaga Vijayaditya, Bhima I or Rajaraja Narendra.
[78:3:9] - **Vishnuvardhana III** granted **Mushikonda** to the Jains; **Ammaraja II** issued the **Maliyapundi** grant (Jain temple, Dharmapuri); courtesan **Chamekamba** won the **Kaluchumbarru** grant.
[78:3:10] - **Dynasty that most propagated Jainism in Telugu land = the Vemulawada Chalukyas** (Welfare Officers 2017 ×2) – patrons of **Pampa** and Somadeva Suri; Baddega built the Subhadhama Jinalaya – not the Eastern, Badami or Kalyani Chalukyas.
[78:3:11] ~~ Sources: NextGen Eastern Chalukyas (src/ap-history/nextgen-06-eastern-chalukyas.pdf) p.1, p.9-10, p.12, p.14, p.20, p.27-29, p.31; Rocket AP History p.11, p.25; app notes 1:78 (sub 7)
## SUB 4 | Founder, Dynasty Outline and the Chola Connection
[78:4:0] # Founder
[78:4:1] - **Kubja Vishnuvardhana**, **brother of Pulakeshin II**, founded the **Chalukyas of Vengi** (UPPSC 2003) – not Bhanuvardhan, Vijayaditya I or Pulakeshin IV.
[78:4:2] - **Pulakeshin II** took Vengi after defeating the **Vishnukundins** (c. 616); Kubja **viceroy 617**, **independent 624** (JL 2006) – Kopparam plates (**631**) of Pulakeshin II call him **Yuvaraja**; Chipurupalli plates (**Vizianagaram**) of his **18th regnal year**.
[78:4:3] - Titles: **Vishamasiddhi** ("conqueror of difficult places / forts") (APPSC PYQ) – not Jayasimha I, Vijayaditya I/II; also **Makaradhwaja**, Kamadeva, Parama Bhagavata.
[78:4:4] # Identity
[78:4:5] - Branch of the **Badami Chalukyas**; initially **subordinates of Badami**; ruled **624–1075** (over four centuries); emblem **boar (Varaha)**; official language **Sanskrit** (most of ~100 grants); matronymic **Hariti-putra** (like the Satavahanas, Ikshvakus, Kadambas); seal sign manual **Tribhuvanankusa**.
[78:4:6] - **NOT true (ATWO):** they were **not annexed by the Rashtrakutas** – they survived the long Rashtrakuta wars and merged into the **Chola** line.
[78:4:7] - **Contemporaries in the south: the Pallavas** (Jayasimha I clashed with them) – not Ikshvakus (earlier), Mughals or Palas.
[78:4:8] - **Land measures:** **nivartana**, kharidika, kharis = units of **area** (land) (APPSC JA).
[78:4:9] # Rulers and titles in order
[78:4:10] TABLE head: Ruler | Title / event
  [78:4:10.0] Jayasimha I (Vallabha) | Samasta Bhuvanashraya; capital to Vengi; Vipparla
  [78:4:10.1] Kokkili Vikramaditya | An Eastern Chalukya prince; ousted by Vishnuvardhana III, set up a kingdom at Yalamanchili (Welfare Officers)
  [78:4:10.2] Vijayaditya I | Conflict with Dantidurga (Rashtrakuta) begins
  [78:4:10.3] Vishnuvardhana IV | Defeated by Dhruva, who married his daughter Sheela Mahadevi
  [78:4:10.4] Chalukya Bhima I | 360 battles (Pithapuram inscription of Mallappadeva); repelled Krishna II at Niravadyapura and Peruvanguru; court singer and dancer Chellavva, title Gandharva-Vidya-Visarada
  [78:4:10.5] Vijayaditya IV | Kollabhiganda (G2 2012; APPSC PYQ); ruled six months; died at Virajapuri fighting Kalinga – not Vijayaditya II, Gunaga or Chalukya Bhima
  [78:4:10.6] Ammaraja I | Rajamahendra; Chekurru plate
  [78:4:10.7] Danarnava | Magallu inscription; killed by Jatachoda Bhima
  [78:4:10.8] Saktivarma I | Chalukya Chandra; with Chola help beat Bayyalanambi of Satyasraya (1006)
  [78:4:10.9] Vimaladitya | Rajamartanda, Mummadi Bhima; married Kundavai; crowned 1011
  [78:4:10.10] Rajaraja Narendra | Crowned 1022; married Ammanga Devi (Rajendra Chola's daughter); after Koppam (1053) accepted Kalyani suzerainty
  [78:4:10.11] Vijayaditya VII | Last king; ousted Rajendra Chalukya in 1070; died 1075
[78:4:11] - Succession war: **Rajaraja Narendra** (son of Kundavai, backed by **Rajendra I**) vs **Vijayaditya VII** (son of Melama, backed by Kalyani Jayasimha II); **Rajadhiraja I** won at **Dharanikota**, burnt **Kollipaka**, was killed at **Koppam** by **Ahavamalla Someshwara**.
[78:4:12] - After **973** the main rival was the **Kalyani Chalukyas**.
[78:4:13] # Chola connection and the end
[78:4:14] - The **Cholas kept close political and matrimonial ties with the Chalukyas of Vengi** (G1 Re-exam 2010; G1 PYQ) – not the Pandyas or the Badami/Kalyani Chalukyas.
[78:4:15] - **Rajendra Chalukya = Kulottunga I** (married **Madhurantaki**, daughter of **Rajendra II**) united the two lines – first Chalukya-Chola king; the **Chalukya-Chola era / Mandalika Yugam** (1076–c.1210, Velanati Chodas) followed.
[78:4:16] - Andhra order: **Eastern Chalukyas → Kakatiyas → Reddis → Vijayanagara**; **Kesari Samudra** (Kesamudram) lake = Kakatiya **Prola I**.
[78:4:17] ~~ Sources: NextGen Eastern Chalukyas (src/ap-history/nextgen-06-eastern-chalukyas.pdf) p.1-3, p.7-12, p.15, p.17-19, p.23, p.33-34; Rocket Indian History sheet #145 (rocket-indian-history-02.pdf) p.123; PMF Ancient & Medieval p.116-117; app notes 1:78 (sub 0-4, 9, 10)
[78:4:18] - **Rajaraja Narendra's titles:** **Kavyageetha Priyudu** (lover of poetry), Rajarajanarayana.
## SUB 5 | Vijayaditya II (Narendra Mrigaraja) – the 108 Shiva Temples
[78:5:0] - **Title Narendra Mrigaraja ("lion among kings") = Vijayaditya II** (APPSC PYQ; Welfare Officers 2017) – not Vishnuvardhana IV, Gunaga Vijayaditya or Chalukya Bhima; also Chalukya Rama, Vikramadhavala.
[78:5:1] - **108 Shiva temples – the Narendreswara / Narendra Mrigeswara-alayas = Vijayaditya II** (G2 2008 ×2, 2012, 2019; G2 PYQ; APPSC PYQ) – built at the sites of his **108 battles in 12 years** with the Rashtrakutas (Govinda III, Amoghavarsha), **as penance**; recorded in the **Sataluru** inscription.
[78:5:2]   - **⚠ Settled:** one G2 printed key gave **Vijayaditya I**; the king is **Vijayaditya II** (when he is missing from the options, the correct answer is added).
[78:5:3]   - Not Kubja Vishnuvardhana, Vishnuvardhana III/IV, Gunaga Vijayaditya or Chalukya Bhima (Bhima I = 360 battles).
[78:5:4] - He overthrew his brother **Bhima Salki** and took the throne (c. 808/818).
[78:5:5] ~~ Sources: NextGen Eastern Chalukyas (src/ap-history/nextgen-06-eastern-chalukyas.pdf) p.2, p.7, p.12, p.29; Rocket AP History p.25, p.47; app notes 1:78 (sub 2, 7)
